summary: Discrepant throttle exposure observed during concurrent batch -> streaming migration
description: Issue summary: Customer migrated a set of workers from a bulk batch ingestion flow to a low-latency streaming flow in their dedicated pool. Shortly after migration they observed repeated 429 responses for a subset of API keys while other keys on the same tenant remained healthy. Impact: production traffic serving low-latency chat experiences saw 15-20% of streaming requests receive 429s for ~2 hours, user-facing errors and increased retries. Hypothesis: disparity in token accounting between batch and streaming route layers combined with per-key burst smoothing is causing uneven refill behavior after the migration.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use InsightMetrics prod tenant in us-east dedicated pool
2) Start sustained batch embedding job using api key A at 300 rps for 10 minutes
3) Rotate a subset of worker clients to streaming protocol using api key B and open multiplexed websocket connections (50 concurrent streams)
4) Observe 429s returned from /v1/streams/start and intermittent 429s on text generation endpoints within 2 minutes of switch
logs: Gateway logs show health-check probes from edge-proxy ip 34.82.11.9 incrementing tenant counters during warmup window
Dedicated pool autoscaler log: scale_event at 2026-03-10T09:11:30Z - no capacity change
investigation_notes: Support reproduced locally against a staging replica with a dedicated-pool config; observed that multiplexed websocket sessions consume per-connection concurrency windows plus per-key token refill accounting.

Rate-limiter team: smoothing algorithm uses a 60s refill window and a short 'burst credit' bucket that is applied per-route and per-key; when clients move from a bulk delayed-retry pattern to many short-lived stream starters the burst credit is consumed unevenly and refill appears skewed due to fractional accounting rounding.

Edge proxy health-checks: confirmed that default health probes on some customers were routed through the tenant's route and incrementing token counters; recommended disabling tenant-scoped probes or routing them through a dedicated health route.

Confirmed that key-A (batch) retained large steady token consumption but batch path marks tokens as 'sustained' which allows smoothing to re-balance; streaming path marks tokens as 'interactive' and immediate accounting leads to earlier exhaustion of the burst bucket for key-B.

Observed mismatch between console quota readout and runtime: console displayed updated quotas after tier changes but runtime token refill used cached window config for ~90s due to config propagation TTL; potential contributing factor during this migration window.
resolution_notes: Short-term workaround: recommended InsightMetrics stagger startup of streaming clients (5s jitter) and raise streaming per-key burst cap via console for the tenant while we push a runtime fix.
Applied a temporary config change at 2026-03-11T02:04Z: increased per-key streaming burst allowance from 200 to 600 for tenant InsightMetrics; reported 429s fell below 1% within 8 minutes.

Medium-term fix: rate-limiter team to deploy a patch that aligns per-route accounting semantics for batch vs interactive paths and reduces rounding skew for fractional token refills. Patch PR: github.com/redwood/rate-control/pull/231 (pending review).
Follow-ups: create console indicator for 'pending config propagation' TTL and add runbook step to route health checks off tenant token counters.
